title: Privilege Resolution
description_html:
Assume in a system, you can grant access by assigning allowed privileges (e.g. "A", "B", "C") to a role, or explicitly block access by specifying disallowed privileges for a role. And a role (the granted role) can be granted to another role (the grantee role). The grantee role can inherit the privileges that the granted role is allowed.

If you are given a role hierarchy tree and allowed/disallowed privileges for each role, find all allowed privileges of each role in the hierarchy.

Input

  • The hierarchy has n roles numbered 0..n-1.
  • grants[i] = [fromi, toi] — there is a grant from fromi to toi.
  • allowedList[i] — the explicitly allowed privileges for role i.
  • disallowedList[i] — the explicitly disallowed privileges for role i.
  • Privileges are letters A–Z.

Output

Return a list answer where answer[i] is the set of allowed privileges of role i.

Approach hint

Treat grants as a DAG (from → to). Topologically sort, then for each role X in topo order:

effective[X] = allowedList[X] ∪ ⋃ effective[Y]  for each (Y → X) ∈ grants
effective[X] -= disallowedList[X]

Represent each set as a 26-bit bitmask (privileges are A–Z) — union becomes OR, subtract becomes AND-NOT. O((V + E) · α) where α is constant for 26 bits.

Closest LC patterns: LC 2192 (All Ancestors of a Node in a DAG) — direct ancestor-set propagation; LC 1857 (Largest Color Value in a Directed Graph) — DAG + topo + per-category propagation; LC 1462 (Course Schedule IV) — transitive closure.
